content.value_statement: SEO teams need clear reasons why competitors outrank them. This skill structures ranking signal analysis, competitive gaps, and action plans.
actual_capabilities: Estimate Q*, P*, and T* ranking signals for a target keyword.
Compare page quality, content coverage, authority, and trust signals against competitors.
Assess NavBoost signals such as click-through rate, dwell time, skip rate, and pogo-sticking.
Review E-E-A-T factors, including expertise, authority, trust, citations, and author credibility.
Plan SEO audits with technical, content, authority, and 90-day action sections.
Recommend keyword targeting strategies based on current ranking position and competitive difficulty.
limitations: It provides frameworks and estimates, not guaranteed ranking outcomes.
It does not include real-time ranking tracking.
It requires reliable SEO data from users or connected tools.
It does not automate backlink prospecting or link building.

use_cases.title: Founder Keyword Decisions
use_cases.description: Decide whether a new business should target a competitive keyword now or start with easier long-tail opportunities.

use_cases.title: SEO Manager Gap Review
use_cases.description: Compare a page against top competitors and turn content, authority, and trust gaps into prioritized work.

use_cases.title: Content Team Audit Planning
use_cases.description: Build an audit roadmap that covers technical checks, content inventory, E-E-A-T, and action priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Keyword
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze whether we should target [keyword]. Use our site context: [brief context]. Estimate difficulty and suggest next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Ranking Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our URL [url] with competitors [urls] for [keyword]. Focus on content completeness, search intent, and E-E-A-T gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full SEO Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full SEO audit plan for [site]. Cover technical, content, authority, trust, timeline, and deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Competitive Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Given rankings [positions], keywords [list], and competitors [list], create a 90-day SEO strategy with priorities and risk notes.

output_examples.input: Analyze a keyword before we invest in content.
output: Recommended target, delay, or long-tail plan.

output_examples.input: Review why our product comparison page is not ranking.
output: Actions ordered by impact and effort.

output_examples.input: Create an SEO audit roadmap for a site.
output: Deliverables for technical, content, and authority work.
Priority recommendations for the next 90 days.

best_practices: Provide target keywords, your URL, competitor URLs, and current ranking data.
Ask for assumptions when SEO metrics are missing or outdated.
Use recommendations as planning inputs and verify them with analytics data.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated ranking signals as guaranteed search engine behavior.
Using the skill without competitor examples or reliable keyword context.
Requesting automated backlink outreach or link-building execution.

faq.question: Does this skill replace SEO tools?
faq.answer: No. It organizes analysis and strategy. Use SEO platforms for fresh rankings, backlinks, and traffic data.

faq.question: Can it analyze real websites?
faq.answer: It can guide website analysis when you provide URLs or tool data. Live inspection depends on available browsing and SEO integrations.

faq.question: What are Q*, P*, and T* signals?
faq.answer: They are planning labels for query intent, page quality, and trust factors in the skill framework.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it guarantee first-page rankings?
faq.answer: No. Search rankings depend on competition, authority, content quality, and many external factors.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide keywords, current URLs, competitor URLs, ranking positions, analytics data, and business goals.
